reasons: Fallback is complete: professional and workmanlike Services standard, software conformance to documentation for 90 days, Services conformance for 30 days measured from performance, and repair/replacement/refund remedies are all express.

Preferred is not met: software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, Services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty — consistent with the locked fallback target.
Minimality holds: a single concise new Section 15.5 was inserted where no performance warranty existed, with no rewrite of 15.2/15.4 and no re-performance or other add-on remedy.

Intent concern: the insertion relies on capitalised "Services" (and "software supplied by Array"), neither of which is a defined term in this license/development agreement, so the warranty scope and the 30-day trigger "following performance of the Services" are potentially dangling; a lower-case description tied to Array's activities under the Agreement (or a definition cross-reference) would cure this.
